subject: Grace period exception and offboard runbook — MSA/order form redlines
messages:

Cc: Acme Procurement <procurement@acme.com>
Date: 2027-02-14T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Questions on auto-renew and termination for convenience

Hi Nikhil,

Thanks for the draft MSA and order form. Procurement reviewed the auto-renew and the termination-for-convenience clauses and they have pushback on two points: (1) the 90-day outside notice for automatic renewal feels long for our fiscal planning — they asked if we can shorten the opt-out window or agree a clear grace period for pilot/POC deals, and (2) they want an explicit termination-for-convenience right with a 30-day notice and proportional refund for any remaining committed months.

Can you confirm whether Redwood is open to an exception for pilot/early-stage customers or whether we can propose alternative language that gives Acme safe offboarding? They also requested an offboard runbook listing data export timelines, log retention, and support handoff.

Appreciate a quick turnaround — procurement needs proposed language by end of week to keep finance on schedule.

Best,
Emma Jones
Head of Cloud Partnerships
Acme Analytics

From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-02-15T08:45:00-08:00
Subject: FW: Questions on auto-renew and termination for convenience — redline asks

Team — forwarding Acme's asks. Key ask: shorten opt-out window for renewal (or carveout for pilot) + termination-for-convenience with 30 days and pro-rated refund. Procurement wants proposed language by EOD Thursday.

Laura — can you draft the offboard runbook and include: data export format/options, time to export, log retention post-termination, contact matrix, and uplift support estimates?

Rishi — high level guidance welcome. My suggested compromise to start the legal draft:
- Auto-renew: standard renewal term remains 12 months but customer may elect non-renewal if notice provided at least 60 days prior to renewal date (instead of 90). For pilot/order forms under $50k TCV, allow a 30-day notice opt-out.
- Termination for convenience: allow mutual termination for convenience with 90 days' notice for enterprise contracts; for pilots only, customer may terminate for convenience with 30 days' notice subject to payment of fees for a defined wind-down period (e.g., remainder of current month + 30 days).

Please advise edits to that approach and any mandatory carveouts (SLA, minimum commitments). I attached the latest MSA redline we have.

Thanks — Nikhil

Attachments: Redwood_MSA_redline_v3.pdf

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-02-15T13:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: FW: Questions on auto-renew and termination for convenience — redline asks

Nikhil / Laura — quick legal read: your suggested compromise is workable with clean redline language. High-level guidance below (summarized for non-legal audience):

1) Auto-renewal / opt-out window
- Maintain default 12-month renewal but shorten opt-out window to 60 days for standard orders.
- For low-TCV pilots (< $50k) propose a special order-form clause: "Pilot orders may be terminated or non-renewed with 30 days' prior written notice." Include explicit definition of "Pilot Order" in order form (start/end dates or TCV threshold).

Suggested wording (MSA):
"Either party may elect not to renew the then-current Subscription Term by providing written notice to the other party not less than sixty (60) days prior to the end of the then-current Subscription Term. Notwithstanding the foregoing, orders expressly identified in the applicable Order Form as 'Pilot Orders' are subject to a separate renewal and termination regimen set forth in such Order Form, which may include a thirty (30) day notice period for non-renewal."

2) Termination for convenience
- We should be cautious about an unrestricted 30-day customer termination right on enterprise commitments. Counter-offer: enterprise contracts — mutual termination for convenience with 90 days' notice and obligation to pay any non-cancellable committed fees through the 90-day wind-down (or parties may agree a pro-rata calculation).
- For pilot orders, allow a customer termination for convenience with 30 days' notice. Require customer to pay (a) any unpaid fees for services already delivered and (b) a one-month wind-down fee to cover transition costs. This preserves predictability without overexposing Redwood.

3) Offboard / data export runbook
- Acceptable to provide a runbook as an attachment to the SOW/order form and to make specific SLAs (e.g., export within 15 business days; logs retained for 90 days post-termination unless otherwise agreed).
- Add a short clause that Redwood will provide reasonable cooperation for data export but may charge for extraordinary data extraction beyond normal exports.

4) Operational language to include in order form
- Define Pilot Order, include TCV thresholds, and list the special termination/notice mechanics.

I'll produce a redline snippet for the MSA and a template clause for the order form.

Rishi Malhotra
Senior Counsel | Redwood Inference

From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Jones <emma.jones@acme.com>, Acme Procurement <procurement@acme.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-02-16T15:43:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Questions on auto-renew and termination for convenience — proposed compromise and runbook

Emma — thanks for the patience. Per our internal review (below) here's the consolidated proposal we can put in your MSA/order form:

1) Renewal mechanics
- Standard orders: 12-month renewal term; customer must give written notice of non-renewal at least sixty (60) days prior to the end of the then-current term.
- Pilot Orders: orders identified as "Pilot Order" in the Order Form (TCV < $50k or identified with explicit pilot dates) may be non-renewed with thirty (30) days' prior written notice.

2) Termination for convenience
- Enterprise / standard orders: mutual termination for convenience allowed with ninety (90) days' prior written notice. Customer will be responsible for any non-cancellable committed fees or a pro-rata payment covering the ninety (90) day wind-down as measured by the fees in the then-current order form.
- Pilot Orders: customer may terminate for convenience with thirty (30) days' notice; customer will be responsible for unpaid fees for services delivered plus a one-month wind-down fee to cover transition costs.

3) Offboard runbook (attached)
- Laura has drafted an operational runbook that lists: export formats (Parquet/CSV), export SLA (15 business days), log retention (90 days), contact matrix, and estimated uplift costs. See attached MSA_offboard_runbook.xlsx.

4) Next steps
- We attached the redline snippet to the MSA and a pilot-order clause for your Order Form. If procurement is comfortable with the pilot carveout and opt-out timing, we can route a final order form with the pilot clause and the attached runbook for signature.

Would you like a 30-min call tomorrow to walk procurement through the runbook and language? If yes, send availability and we'll lock it in.

Best,
Nikhil Sharma
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Cc: Laura Bennett — Customer Success Manager (attached runbook)
